name_note: GTDB's Butyricimonas virosa also contains genomes that NCBI labels Butyricimonas paravirosa.

sentences.text: Butyricimonas virosa was proposed, with Butyricimonas synergistica, for two strains isolated from rat faeces: obligately anaerobic, non-motile, Gram-negative rods of the family Porphyromonadaceae.
The two strains produced significant levels of butyric and isobutyric acids as end products from glucose, and their major menaquinone was MK-10.
A review describes Butyricimonas species as Gram-negative, anaerobic bacteria that are part of the human gut microbiota, with infections by them extremely rare in clinical practice.
That review compiled 14 publications describing Butyricimonas infections in 14 patients, with a history of malignancy the most frequently reported predisposing factor.
In mice fed a high-fat diet, a study reported that oral gavage of Butyricimonas virosa suppressed progression of steatotic liver disease and enhanced production of thiamine monophosphate.
